chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you seeks a need, let him praise his Lord and extol Him, for when a man seeks a need from a ruler, he prepares for him the best speech he is able to muster.'

So when you seek a need, glorify Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, and praise Him and extol Him, saying: 'O the Most Generous of those who give, and O the Best of those who are asked, O the Most Merciful of those who are shown mercy, O the One, O the Eternal, O He who did not beget nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, O He who took no companion and no son, O He who does what He wills and decrees what He desires and ordains what He loves, O He who turns between a man and his heart, O He who is at the Exalted View, O He who is like nothing else, O the All-Hearing, O the All-Seeing!'

And frequent the Names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the Names of Allah are many, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny, and say: 'O Allah, expand upon me from Your permissible sustenance that which I can suffice with, and repay with regarding my trust, and connect with my kinship, and it be a help to me in Hajj and Umrah.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man entered the mosque, prayed two cycles, then asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Then another came, prayed two cycles, then praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sent blessings upon the Prophet and his Progeny. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and formula for making a supplication in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *al-hamd* (praise) and *al-du'a* (supplication) as a structured protocol, drawing an analogy to courtly etiquette where one prepares eloquent praise before making a request to a sovereign. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on utilizing the Beautiful Names (*Asma al-Husna*) to align the supplicant’s heart with divine attributes before asking, thereby transforming the act of asking into an act of worship. The concluding narrative reinforces that hastiness in petitioning is less effective than first establishing a spiritual connection through glorification and blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt.
